f.title: Put an appropriate safety monitoring system in place for registered products
f.statement: Each MAH of registered products shall put in place an appropriate system of safety monitoring in order to assume responsibility and liability for its products on the market and to ensure appropriate action can be taken when necessary.
f.clause: 5.1 Pharmacovigilance systems and their quality systems

rows.quote: An appropriate system of safety monitoring shall be put in place by each Marketing Authorization Holder of registered products in order to assume responsibility and liability for products on the market
rows.location: 5.1 Pharmacovigilance systems and their quality systems
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Actively monitor product safety in clinical practice for the period the Authority specifies
f.statement: In addition to spontaneous ADR reporting, the MAH shall put in place pharmacovigilance measures to actively monitor the safety of its products in clinical practice for a period specified by the Authority.
f.clause: 5.1 Pharmacovigilance systems and their quality systems

rows.deadline: For the period specified by the Authority

rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Have a QPPV permanently and continuously available
f.statement: The MAH shall permanently and continuously have at its disposal an appropriately qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance (QPPV) or responsible personnel for PV.
f.clause: 5.1 Pharmacovigilance systems and their quality systems

rows.quote: The MAH shall permanently and continuously have at his disposal an appropriately Qualified Person Responsible for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) or Responsible Personnel for PV.
rows.location: 5.1 Pharmacovigilance systems and their quality systems
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Include the minimum components in the PV system
f.statement: The MAH's PV system should consist at least of: collection and management of product safety data including individual ADR reporting; a signal detection system for new or changing safety issues; data evaluation and decision-making on safety issues; proactive risk management; action to protect public health (including regulatory action); and communication with stakeholders and the public.
f.clause: 5.1 Pharmacovigilance systems and their quality systems

rows.quote: Pharmacovigilance system of market authorization holder should consist at least of the following:
rows.location: 5.1 Pharmacovigilance systems and their quality systems
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Treat the listed PV processes as critical
f.statement: The following PV processes should be considered critical: continuous safety profile monitoring and benefit-risk evaluation; risk management systems and evaluation of risk-minimisation effectiveness; ICSR collection, processing, quality control, follow-up, coding, duplicate detection, evaluation and timely electronic transmission; PSUR scheduling, preparation, submission and assessment; meeting commitments and responding to Authority requests; interaction between PV and product quality defect systems; safety communication with the Authority (in particular changes to the benefit-risk balance) and with patients and HCPs; keeping product information up to date; and implementing safety variations according to urgency.

rows.quote: The following pharmacovigilance processes should be considered as critical:
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Allocate fit-for-purpose PV facilities and equipment and qualify critical ones
f.statement: Appropriate facilities and equipment (office space, IT systems, storage space) shall be allocated to support PV processes; they should be fit for their intended purpose, and facilities and equipment critical for PV should be subject to periodic checks, qualification and/or validation.
f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Validation & change control

rows.quote: Appropriate facilities and equipment shall be allocated to support pharmacovigilance processes and their outcomes.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Establish a PV quality system covering the quality cycle
f.statement: MAHs are required to establish a quality system for all PV activities, covering organisational structure, responsibilities, procedures, processes and resources, and involving quality planning, adherence, control, assurance and improvement; it shall include quality documentation, record management, training, stakeholder communication and continuous improvement.

rows.quote: MAHs are required to establish a quality system for all pharmacovigilance activities to produce desired outcome and quality objectives.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Management ensures documented quality system, resources, reviews, escalation and audits
f.statement: Managerial staff should ensure that the organisation documents the quality system under document control; adequate resources, training, premises, facilities and equipment; adequate compliance and record management; risk-based periodic review of the PV and quality system with corrective and preventive measures; timely communication and escalation of safety concerns and investigation of suspected non-adherence; and that audits are performed.
f.clause: 5.1.3.3 Responsibilities for the quality system within an organisation

rows.quote: managerial staff (i.e. staff with management responsibilities) in any organisation should be responsible for:
rows.location: 5.1.3.3 Responsibilities for the quality system within an organisation
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Have quality procedures ensuring monitoring, evaluation, accurate timely reporting and communication
f.statement: The PV quality system should have procedures ensuring: continuous monitoring of PV data and risk-minimisation measures; scientific evaluation of all risk information; submission of accurate, verifiable serious and non-serious ADR data within legal time limits; quality, integrity and completeness of submitted information, avoiding duplicate submissions and validating signals; effective communication with authorities; updating product information; and communication of safety information to HCPs and patients.

rows.quote: the submission of accurate and verifiable data on serious and non-serious adverse reactions to the competent authorities within the legally required time-limits.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Document the quality system in policies, procedures, plans and records
f.statement: All quality system elements shall be documented systematically in written policies and procedures (quality plans, manuals, records). The quality system shall be documented by: organisational structures and task assignments; training plans and records; compliance management instructions; instructions for urgent situations including business continuity; performance indicators; and reports of quality audits and follow-up audits. Training plans and records shall be kept and made available for audit and inspection.

rows.quote: All elements, requirements and provisions adopted for the quality system shall be documented in a systematic and orderly manner in the form of written policies and procedures, such as quality plans, quality manuals and quality records.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Keep training plans and records available for audit and inspection
f.statement: Training plans and records shall be kept and made available for audit and inspection.

rows.quote: Training plans and records shall be kept and made available for audit and inspection
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Record all PV information and keep a record management system with traceability of safety decisions
f.statement: The MAH shall record all PV information so it allows accurate reporting, interpretation and verification, and shall have a record management system for all PV documents ensuring retrievability and traceability of measures taken to investigate safety concerns, their timelines and decisions, including dates and decision-making process.

rows.quote: A record management system shall be put in place for all documents used for pharmacovigilance activities, ensuring their retrievability as well as traceability of the measures taken to investigate safety concerns, of the timelines for those investigations and of decisions on safety concerns, including their date and the decision-making process.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Support data quality, timely access, communication and retention in the record system
f.statement: The record management system should support management of the quality (completeness, accuracy, integrity) of PV data, timely access to all records, effective internal and external communication, and retention of PV system and product documents in line with applicable retention periods; records should be protected from destruction during the retention period.

rows.quote: There should be appropriate structures and processes in place to ensure that pharmacovigilance data and records are protected from destruction during the applicable record retention period.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Ensure traceability and follow-up of ADR reports with personal data protection
f.statement: MAHs shall establish mechanisms enabling traceability and follow-up of adverse reaction reports, ensuring personal data protection is fully guaranteed, with data security and confidentiality measures at each stage of storage and processing.
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: In addition, marketing authorisation holders shall establish mechanisms enabling the traceability and follow-up of adverse reaction reports.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Designate a QPPV for Zimbabwe; the MAH retains overall responsibility
f.statement: Every MAH with a medicine registered in Zimbabwe shall designate a responsible person for PV or QPPV to oversee the PV system. The MAH retains overall responsibility for its products. The QPPV may reside in Zimbabwe or be external (e.g. a QPPV for a cluster of countries including Zimbabwe, or a Zimbabwe-specific QPPV).

rows.quote: Every MAH who has registered a medicine in Zimbabwe shall designate a responsible person for PV or QPPV to oversee the pharmacovigilance system.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Notify MCAZ in writing of the QPPV, CV, contacts and responsibilities
f.statement: The MAH should notify MCAZ in writing who its responsible person for PV or QPPV is, with curriculum vitae, contact details and responsibilities (Appendix II gives the application form for designation as a QPPV).

rows.quote: For administrative purposes the MAH should notify the MCAZ in writing who their responsible person for PV or the QPPV is, their curriculum vitae, contact details and their responsibilities.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Appoint a QPPV with a healthcare degree and recognised PV training
f.statement: The QPPV should be a healthcare professional (degree in medicine, pharmacy, nursing, biomedical sciences or other recognised healthcare degree), have received formal PV training recognised by the Authority, and know Zimbabwe PV legislation, guidelines and international standards. Training should cover at least PV terminology, PV and quality systems, PSMF, risk management, ICSR management including duplicates and literature searching, signal management, safety communication, PSURs/PBRERs, audits and inspections, and Zimbabwe legislation.

rows.quote: The QPPV should have received a formal training in pharmacovigilance recognized by the Authority and should have knowledge of the Zimbabwe pharmacovigilance legislation and guidelines and other international standards for Pharmacovigilance.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Train the QPPV and give authority, resources and access to information
f.statement: The MAH should provide comprehensive PV training to the QPPV; ensure the QPPV has sufficient authority to implement PV activities and give input into RMPs and regulatory documents on emerging safety concerns; and ensure processes, resources, communication mechanisms and access to all relevant information for the QPPV's tasks.

rows.quote: Ensure that the QPPV has sufficient authority to Implement pharmacovigilance activities
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Notify MCAZ of QPPV absence within 30 days of the vacancy
f.statement: The MAH should notify the Authority of the absence of the QPPV not later than 30 days after the position becomes vacant.

rows.deadline: Not later than 30 days after the position becomes vacant
rows.quote: Notify the Authority of the absence of the QPPV not later than 30 days after the position becomes vacant.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Have a written contract with the QPPV
f.statement: The MAH should have a written contract with the QPPV.

rows.quote: Have a written contract with the QPPV.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV oversees the PV system and is the contact point, available during inspections
f.statement: The QPPV should oversee the structure and functioning of the PV system and act as the point of contact on all PV and product safety matters, including inspections, and be available during PV inspections.

rows.quote: He or she should be available during PV inspections.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV maintains a system collecting all suspected ADRs for submission to MCAZ
f.statement: The QPPV is responsible for establishing and maintaining a system ensuring that information about all suspected ADRs/events reported to MAH personnel and medical representatives is collected, collated and assessed for onward submission to the Authority.
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Establishment and maintenance of a system which ensures that information about all suspected adverse drug reactions/ events which are reported to the personnel of the marketing authorization holder and to the medical representatives is collected, collated and assessed for onward submission to the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV has PSMF access and authority to verify its accuracy
f.statement: The QPPV should have access to the PSMF and be in a position of authority to ensure and verify that it accurately reflects the PV system.

rows.quote: The QPPV should have access to the pharmacovigilance system master file (PSMF) and be in a position of authority to ensure and to verify that the
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: QPPV prepares ICSRs, PSURs, study reports and RMPs and answers MCAZ requests
f.statement: The QPPV provides input into regulatory action on emerging safety concerns (variations, urgent safety restrictions, communications); prepares ICSRs, PSURs/PBRERs when necessary, company-sponsored safety and efficacy study reports and RMPs when necessary; ensures Authority requests for benefit-risk information are answered promptly and fully; and ensures safety monitoring oversight of marketed products and emerging concerns.

rows.quote: Ensure that any request from the Authority for additional information deemed necessary for the evaluation of the risk–benefit afforded by a marketed product, is provided to MCAZ promptly and fully.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Keep the PSMF legible, complete, accessible and traceable
f.statement: The PSMF should be legible, complete, provided in a manner ensuring all documentation is accessible, and allow full traceability of changes. The cover page should give the MAH name, PSMF version number, date of preparation/last update and any service provider managing the PV system.

rows.quote: The PSMF should be legible, complete, provided in a manner that ensures all documentation is accessible and allow full traceability of changes.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Describe the QPPV, back-up and delegated tasks in the PSMF
f.statement: The PSMF QPPV section should include the QPPV's responsibilities and authority, summary CV, contact details and back-up arrangements (with back-up QPPV CV and contacts); a list of tasks delegated by the QPPV, to whom, and access to a medically qualified person shall be included in the Annexes.

rows.quote: A list of tasks that have been delegated by the qualified person for pharmacovigilance shall also be included in the Annexes.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Describe organisational structure, PV sites and subcontracted activities in the PSMF
f.statement: The PSMF shall describe the MAH's organisational structure showing the QPPV's position, the sites where PV functions are performed, and activities or services subcontracted for PV (including in other countries), with a list of contracts and agreements in the annexes; individual agreements should be available to MCAZ on request and at inspection.

rows.quote: The PSMF, where applicable, shall contain a description of the activities and/or services subcontracted by the MAH relating to the fulfilment of pharmacovigilance obligations.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Describe sources of safety data and the ICSR flow in the PSMF
f.statement: The PSMF should describe all units responsible, globally, for solicited and spontaneous case collection (including medical information sites and affiliates, with contact points), the ICSR process from collection to reporting to MCAZ with departments and third parties involved, and study, registry, surveillance or support programme sources.
f.clause: 5.3.1.4 PSMF section on sources of safety data

rows.quote: The description of the process for ICSRs from collection to reporting to MCAZ should indicate the departments and/or third parties involved.
rows.location: 5.3.1.4 PSMF section on sources of safety data
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Describe computerised systems, their validation and fitness for purpose in the PSMF
f.statement: The PSMF shall describe the location, functionality and operational responsibility of computerised systems and databases used to receive, collate, record and report safety information and an assessment of their fitness for purpose, including validation status, change control, testing, back-up and data repositories; for paper-based systems, data management and integrity mechanisms.

rows.quote: The location, functionality and operational responsibility for computerised systems and databases used to receive, collate, record and report safety information and an assessment of their fitness for purpose shall be described in the PSMF.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Describe PV processes in the PSMF with a list of procedural documents
f.statement: The PSMF shall describe the processes, data handling and records for: continuous benefit-risk monitoring and signal management; risk management and monitoring of risk-minimisation outcomes; ICSR collection, follow-up, assessment and reporting (local vs global); PSUR scheduling and submission; safety communication; and implementation of safety variations. The description must be accompanied by a list of processes with document reference, title, effective date and type, identifying third-party procedures.

rows.quote: The description must be accompanied by the list of processes.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Show PV performance monitoring, targets and KPI results in the PSMF
f.statement: The PSMF should contain evidence of ongoing monitoring of PV system performance: how correct ICSR reporting is assessed (with timeliness figures for the past year), quality metrics including MCAZ feedback, PSUR timeliness, methods for timely safety variations including tracking of pending ones, and adherence to RMP commitments. Performance targets shall be described and a list of performance indicators with actual results must be provided in the annex.
f.clause: 5.3.1.7 PSMF section on pharmacovigilance system performance

rows.quote: A list of performance indicators must be provided in the Annex to the PSMF alongside the results of (actual) performance measurements.
rows.location: 5.3.1.7 PSMF section on pharmacovigilance system performance
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Describe the quality system, audits and deviations in the PSMF
f.statement: The PSMF quality section shall cover document and record control (archiving), procedural documents, training (including anyone who may receive safety reports), and auditing, with a list of scheduled and completed audits over a rolling 5-year period and a note for any audit with significant findings; it shall also document deviations from PV procedures, their impact and management until resolved.

rows.quote: The master file shall also document deviations from pharmacovigilance
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Include the required annexes and change history in the PSMF
f.statement: The PSMF annex shall contain: products covered (per active substance, with product-specific monitoring requirements and references to other PSMFs); list of policies and procedures; contractual agreements; tasks delegated by the QPPV; completed audits for five years and audit schedules; and lists of safety data sources. A history of changes to annex contents should record at least the date, person responsible and nature of the change.

rows.quote: An annex to the PSMF shall contain the following documents:
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Use the RMP to monitor risks and keep product information accurate and current
f.statement: Applicants are responsible for ensuring the RMP constantly monitors the risks of their authorised products and reports results to the Authority as required, and for taking all appropriate actions to minimise risks and maximise benefits, including ensuring the accuracy of all company information on the product and promptly updating and communicating it when new information becomes available.

rows.quote: Ensuring that the RMP constantly monitors the risks of its medicinal products issued with marketing authorization in compliance with relevant legislation and reports the results of this, as required, to the Authority;
rows.review_note: Review: "Applicants are responsible for" read as a duty. Double-check: ok.

f.title: Include safety specification, PV plan and risk-minimisation plan in the RMP
f.statement: The RMP shall contain the safety specification (important identified and potential risks and missing information), the pharmacovigilance plan, and the risk-minimisation plan including evaluation of effectiveness; it must also document post-authorisation obligations, what is known and unknown, the need for effectiveness studies, and how risk-minimisation effectiveness will be assessed.
f.clause: 5.4 Risk Management Plans; 5.4.2 Requirements of a RMP

rows.quote: The RMP must contain the following elements which:
rows.location: 5.4 Risk Management Plans; 5.4.2 Requirements of a RMP
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit an RMP only when required, within 90 days of request
f.statement: An RMP shall be submitted only when given as a condition of marketing authorisation or when requested post-authorisation by the Authority because of safety concerns or as deemed necessary; RMP submission should occur within 90 days from the date of request, or as specified by the Authority.

rows.deadline: Within 90 days from the date of request, or as specified by the Authority
rows.quote: RMP submission should occur within 90 days from the date of request, or as specified by the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

deadline_rule.applies_to: RMP submission when requested or imposed

f.title: Follow EMA GVP Module V structure for the RMP
f.statement: The structure and format of the RMP should be in line with EMA GVP Module V (Risk management systems).

rows.quote: The structure and format of the RMP should be in-line with the EMA GVP Module V – Risk management systems.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Provide a Zimbabwe Specific Annex to a global or EU RMP
f.statement: Where a global or EU-RMP is submitted, a summarised Zimbabwe Specific Annex should be included; it is required whenever Zimbabwean implementation differs from the global/EU-RMP. It should cover differences in indications, local epidemiology, local medication-error or other risks, applicability of EU activities, implementation and evaluation of risk minimisation in Zimbabwe, justification of EU activities not implemented, and the local RMP contact person.
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Local PV interfaces

rows.quote: A Zimbabwe Specific Annex is required whenever there are differences between the Zimbabwean implementation of the RMP and what is proposed in the global or EU-RMP.
rows.review_note: Review: required when differences exist, otherwise recommended. Double-check: level Mandatory for the "required" case.

f.title: Accompany every RMP with a signed implementation declaration
f.statement: All RMPs submitted shall be accompanied by a declaration signed by the applicant stating it has read the RMP and will ensure implementation of all activities outlined in it.

rows.quote: All RMPs submitted shall be accompanied by a declaration signed by the Applicant.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit PSURs/PBRERs only when imposed or requested
f.statement: PSURs/PBRERs should be submitted only for products registered in Zimbabwe given that condition at authorisation (e.g. new chemical entities) or post-registration as deemed necessary by the Authority; MCAZ may request them when a new concern affecting the benefit-risk profile is identified.

rows.quote: PSUR/PBRERs submission to MCAZ is required only when stated as a condition for Market Authorisation (MA) for a New Chemical entity (NCE) or any product as deemed necessary by the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Follow the PSUR periodicity when imposed as a condition
f.statement: When imposed as a condition of registration, PSURs/PBRERs should be submitted every 6 months for the first two years, yearly for the following 2 years, and at 3-year intervals thereafter, unless otherwise specified.

rows.deadline: 6-monthly for 2 years, yearly for 2 years, then 3-yearly
rows.quote: Every 6 months for the first two years, yearly for the following 2 years, and at 3-year intervals thereafter.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit PSURs within 70 days of DLP for intervals up to 12 months
f.statement: PSURs/PBRERs covering intervals up to and including 12 months must be submitted within 70 calendar days of the data lock point (day 0).

rows.deadline: Within 70 calendar days of the data lock point
rows.quote: within 70 calendar days of the data lock point (day 0) for PSURs/PBRERs covering intervals up to 12 months (including intervals of exactly 12 months); and
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit PSURs within 90 days of DLP for intervals over 12 months
f.statement: PSURs/PBRERs covering intervals in excess of 12 months must be submitted within 90 calendar days of the data lock point (day 0).

rows.deadline: Within 90 calendar days of the data lock point
rows.quote: within 90 calendar days of the data lock point (day 0) for PSURs/PBRERs covering intervals in excess of 12 months
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Present PSURs/PBRERs in ICH E2C(R2) format
f.statement: PSUR and PBRER information shall be presented in the format recommended by ICH E2C(R2) and its Q&As; the E2C(R2) format should be used for all PBRERs, non-applicable sections should be stated, and PSUR structure should follow EMA GVP Module VII.
f.systems: ICH E2C(R2); EMA GVP Module VII

rows.quote: Presentation of the information contained in the PSUR and PBRER shall be in the format recommended by ICH E2C (R2) and ICH E2C (R2) Questions and Answers (Q&As) guidelines respectively.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit reference-agency PSUR assessment reports instead of full PSURs
f.statement: Under the reliance model, for PSURs/PBRERs also submitted to reference stringent regulatory agencies such as EMA, the summarised assessment reports, feedback or correspondence from those agencies should be submitted to the Authority, and full PSUR/PBRER reports should not be submitted.

rows.quote: summarised assessment reports and or feedback reports/responses or correspondences concerning the PSUR/PBRER from such agencies should be submitted to the Authority and in such cases full reports for PSUR/PBRER should not be submitted.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Synchronise PSUR dates with the IBD; longer-cycle PSURs accepted
f.statement: The MAH may synchronise the local birth date with the international birth date; MCAZ accepts a single harmonised IBD and DLP, and where MCAZ requires six-monthly reports but the MAH prepares annual or longer reports for other authorities, the most recent longer-period PSUR is acceptable.

rows.quote: the MAH may synchronize the Local Birth Date (LBD) with the International Birth Date (IBD).
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit ad hoc PSURs within the requested time or 90 days of DLP
f.statement: When MCAZ requests an ad hoc PSUR/PBRER (new or changed risks, changed efficacy or benefit-risk), it should be submitted within the timeline in the request, otherwise within 90 calendar days of the data lock point.

rows.deadline: As specified in the request, otherwise within 90 calendar days of the data lock point
rows.quote: otherwise, the ad hoc PSURs should be submitted within 90 calendar days of the data lock point.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Have PASS protocols approved by ethics committees and MCAZ and run them under MASCA and GCP
f.statement: The study protocol for post-authorisation studies should be approved by the relevant ethics committees (such as MRCZ) and the Authority, and the study conducted in line with MASCA and its regulations, the clinical trial application guidelines and Zimbabwe GCP guidelines, in a Zimbabwean population or one agreed with the Authority.
f.legal_basis: Medicines and Allied Substances Control Act [Chapter 15:03]

rows.quote: The study protocol for Post Authorization Studies should be approved by the relevant Ethics Committees such as MRCZ and the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Do not start a PASS before MCAZ approves the protocol
f.statement: The applicant bears sole responsibility for all regulatory and technical aspects of the PASS, shall develop the protocol in the format prescribed by the Authority, and shall ensure the PASS does not commence before the protocol is approved by the Authority.

rows.quote: The Applicant shall ensure that the PASS study does not commence before the protocol for the study is approved by the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Obtain approval for PASS amendments; report urgent safety amendments within 48 hours
f.statement: All PASS protocol amendments shall be submitted to the ethics committee(s) and the Authority for approval before implementation; where needed to protect patient safety, an amendment may be implemented with the Authority informed immediately by phone, followed by a written report within 48 hours. Amendment reports shall include the reasons and possible consequences for subjects and for the evaluation.

rows.deadline: Phone call immediately; written report within 48 hours
rows.quote: where such amendments are needed to protect the safety of patients, this may be carried out and the Authority informed immediately by phone call, followed by a written report within 48 hours.

f.title: Submit annual PASS progress reports and a final report within 90 days of completion
f.statement: The applicant shall submit annual study progress reports (status, enrolment start date, numbers enrolled and withdrawn with reasons, expected completion) and a final study report not later than 90 days after completion of the study.

rows.deadline: Annual progress reports; final report not later than 90 days after study completion

f.title: Conduct PASS per approved protocol containing the required sections, including AE management
f.statement: All PASS must be conducted according to the approved protocol, which shall include title, applicant, responsible parties, abstract, amendments, milestones, rationale, research question, methods, design, setting, variables, data sources, study size, data management, data analysis, quality control (including records storage and archiving of statistical programmes), limitations, protection of subjects, management and reporting of adverse events/reactions, dissemination plans and references.

f.title: Monitor PASS data for benefit-risk impact and notify new information within 7 days
f.statement: The applicant shall monitor data generated during the study and consider implications for the benefit-risk balance; any new information that may affect it should be communicated to the Authority by official letter to the Director-General within 7 days (study results otherwise go into PSURs/PBRERs and RMP updates).
f.clause: 5.6.8.1 Data relevant to the risk-benefit balance

f.title: Report study adverse reactions to MCAZ with procedures summarised in the protocol
f.statement: Adverse reactions/events in PASS should be reported to the Authority, with collection, management and reporting procedures put in place and summarised in the protocol; ADR reports should be submitted electronically on the MCAZ e-PV platform (or on MCAZ forms).
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Investigator alerts MCAZ of fatal or life-threatening unexpected events within 7 days
f.statement: For clinical trials authorised in Zimbabwe, ICSR submission is the principal investigator's responsibility: fatal or life-threatening unexpected events must be alerted to MCAZ as soon as possible and no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the investigator that a case qualifies.
f.applicability: Clinical trials (and studies) authorised in Zimbabwe

rows.deadline: No later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the investigator
rows.quote: the principal investigator (PI) is required to alert the MCAZ as soon as possible but no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the investigator that a case qualifies

f.title: Follow with a complete report within 8 additional days including an assessment
f.statement: The 7-day alert must be followed by a complete report as soon as possible within 8 additional calendar days, including an assessment of the importance and implications of the findings and relevant previous experience with the same or similar products.
f.applicability: Clinical trials (and studies) authorised in Zimbabwe

rows.deadline: Within 8 additional calendar days after the 7-day alert

f.title: Report other serious unexpected reactions within 15 days of first knowledge
f.statement: Serious unexpected reactions that are not fatal or life-threatening must be filed as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after first knowledge by the principal investigator that the case meets the minimum criteria for expedited reporting.
f.applicability: Clinical trials (and studies) authorised in Zimbabwe

rows.deadline: No later than 15 calendar days after first knowledge

f.title: Submit preliminary report within 30 days and comprehensive safety report within 90 days of trial completion
f.statement: The principal investigator must submit annual progress, preliminary, final reports and publications. Under MASCA, not later than 30 days after completion the person who conducted the trial shall submit a preliminary report on the ethical evaluation, and not later than 90 days after completion a comprehensive report of any serious or adverse effects or reactions established by the trial.

f.title: Notify study discontinuation within 7 working days and submit the final report within 90 days
f.statement: If a study is discontinued, the applicant should inform the Authority with reasons within 7 working days and submit a final report no later than 90 days; monitoring reports and annual renewal applications are submitted at the start of each calendar year.

rows.deadline: 7 working days to notify; final report within 90 days
rows.quote: If a study is discontinued, the applicant should inform the Authority with reasons for the termination within 7 working days and a final report should be submitted no later than 90 days.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Communicate PASS results that affect the RMP or MA and describe the changes
f.statement: Where PASS results affect the risk management system or the marketing authorisation, this shall be communicated to the Authority with the steps to incorporate the changes into the RMP and a variation to the MA.
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote: Where the result of the PASS affects the risk management system or the marketing authorization status of the medicinal product, this shall be communicated to the Authority

f.title: Have post-authorisation efficacy studies approved and run as for PASS
f.statement: All post-authorisation studies, including PAES, should be approved by the ethics committees and the Authority; PASS requirements in sections 5.6.3-5.6.8 apply to PAES.

rows.quote: All Post Authorization Studies should be approved by the Ethics Committees and the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Report serious ADRs occurring in Zimbabwe within 15 calendar days
f.statement: The pharmaceutical industry should report all serious ADRs occurring in Zimbabwe, expected or unexpected, as soon as possible and no later than 15 calendar days of initial receipt of the information.

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 15 calendar days of initial receipt
rows.quote: Pharmaceutical industry should report all serious adverse drug reactions occurring in Zimbabwe (whether expected or unexpected) as soon as possible, but in no case later than 15 calendar days of initial receipt of the information.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit an initial report with minimum data and follow up later
f.statement: If not all information is available within 15 days, the applicant should submit an initial report with at least the minimum data elements (patient, suspected product, reaction and reporter details) to meet the timeline, followed by a more detailed follow-up report as soon as available.

rows.quote: the Applicant should submit an initial report containing at least the minimum data elements required (i.e., patient details, suspected product details, reaction details and the reporter details) in order to meet the expedited reporting time frames.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Report non-serious ADRs within 28 calendar days
f.statement: Non-serious ADRs, expected or not, are to be reported to MCAZ as soon as possible, within 28 calendar days of initial receipt of the information.

rows.deadline: Within 28 calendar days of initial receipt
rows.quote: Cases of non-serious ADRs, whether expected or not, are also to be reported to the MCAZ as soon as possible, within a period of 28 calendar days of initial receipt of the information.

f.title: Search Medline/Embase weekly and local journals on schedule for Zimbabwe cases
f.statement: MAHs are required to search widely referenced databases (e.g. Medline, Embase) weekly and submit any case originating from Zimbabwe on registered products, and to search local journals not in those databases on a schedule matching their periodicity; publications should be accompanied by a copy of the article, with an ADR form per identifiable patient and the authors as primary source.

rows.deadline: Weekly searches; same timelines as spontaneous reports
rows.quote: Marketing Authorization Holders are required to search widely referenced databases (e.g., Medline, Embase) on a weekly basis and submit any case originating from Zimbabwe on registered products to the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Handle lay-press and internet reports as spontaneous reports and screen MAH digital media
f.statement: Lay press reports should be handled as spontaneous reports, collecting minimum information for a valid ICSR with the same timelines. Internet or digital media managed by the MAH should be screened regularly and reports submitted within timelines; reports from non-company sites or social media should be assessed against minimum criteria and treated as spontaneous. Safety information from follow-up should also be reported.
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Internet or Digital media under the management of MAH should be screened regularly for adverse reaction reports and report to the Authority within the specified timelines.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit ICSRs in E2B XML by e-mail or via the MCAZ e-PV platform
f.statement: MAHs may send reports in E2B format (.xml) by e-mail to MCAZ or via the E2B(R2)-compatible MCAZ e-PV reporting platform (receiver ID MCAZ).

rows.quote: The file format should be .xml.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Do not submit foreign ICSRs routinely
f.statement: Foreign ICSRs should not be submitted routinely but only in the context of a specific safety issue impacting the benefit-risk profile or on specific request by the Authority.

rows.quote: Foreign individual case safety reports should not be submitted to the Authority on a routine basis but should be reported in the context of a specific safety issue which impacts/changes the risk-benefit profile of the product or on specific request by the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Assess causality of collected adverse events per ICH E2D
f.statement: Collected adverse events should be systematically assessed for possible relationship to the product in line with ICH E2D; MAHs may use their preferred causality method.

rows.quote: The collected adverse events should be systematically assessed to determine whether they are possibly related to the supplied medical products in line with ICH-E2D.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Follow up pregnancy exposures and report pregnancy/breastfeeding ADRs
f.statement: MAHs are expected to follow up all pregnancy reports where the embryo/foetus could have been exposed (considering long half-lives) and must report suspected ADRs related to pregnancy or breastfeeding, whether or not the drug is contraindicated.

rows.quote:
MAHs must report suspected adverse drug reactions related to pregnancy or breastfeeding, regardless of whether the drug is contra-
indicated in pregnancy and/or lactation.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Report lack of efficacy for life-threatening indications with the batch number
f.statement: Lack of efficacy with medicines used for life-threatening conditions where it could have serious consequences should be reported (including unapproved indications), using clinical judgement on seriousness; the batch number must be included.

rows.quote: The batch number of the suspected medicine for a report of lack of efficacy must be included in the report.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Report reactions associated with overdose
f.statement: Reactions associated with an overdose should be reported, including cases where the suspect medicine led to suicidal intention and subsequent overdose.

rows.quote: Reactions associated with an overdose should be reported.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Report off-label use, misuse, abuse and occupational exposure with an ADR
f.statement: Reports of off-label use, misuse, abuse or occupational exposure should be submitted when associated with an adverse reaction, with an additional ADR term reflecting the situation on the ICSR.
f.clause: 5.8.11 Off-label use / misuse / abuse / occupational exposure

rows.quote: An additional ADR term that is reflective of the off-label use / misuse / abuse / occupational exposure should be on the ICSR

rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Record, report and assess all medication errors and summarise them in PSURs and RMPs
f.statement: All medication errors should be reported to the Authority whether serious or not, expected or not, and whether or not ADRs occurred; MAHs should record, report and assess all medication errors brought to their attention, distinguish errors with ADR, without harm, intercepted and potential errors, and summarise patterns in the PSUR and RMP.

rows.quote: All medication errors should be reported to the Authority, whether serious or nonserious, expected or unexpected, suspected ADRs/AEFIs have occurred or not.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Report AEs suspected from medicine defects with batch number and quality actions
f.statement: An adverse event suspected to relate to a medicine defect should be reported like a suspected ADR; the batch number must be included, and the applicant should inform the Authority whether implicated products were tested and what corrective actions were taken. AEs from suspected interactions should be reported as adverse reactions.

rows.quote: The batch number of the suspected medicines must be included in the report.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Perform documented signal management
f.statement: Management of signals is a requirement for MAHs. Signal detection should follow a methodology suited to the data and product type, use all appropriate sources with clinical judgement, and be adequately documented; validation should weigh previous awareness, strength of evidence and clinical relevance; and prioritisation should be performed continuously considering public health impact.

rows.quote: Management of signals is a requirement for marketing authorization holders and NRAs.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Validate new signals and inform MCAZ within 30 days of concluding assessment
f.statement: Where an MAH detects a new signal it shall validate it and inform the Authority forthwith, as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after completing its assessment and concluding that further regulatory analysis is required.

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after completing the assessment
rows.quote: This should be done as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after the MAH has completed their assessment and concluded that further analysis by the regulatory authorities is required.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Notify MCAZ when suspending, withdrawing or cancelling marketing due to an emerging safety issue
f.statement: Emerging safety issues (major issues from studies, spontaneous reports or literature, or major regulatory actions by other NRAs) require urgent attention; if the MAH decides as a result to suspend, withdraw or cancel marketing of the product, it shall notify the Authority.

rows.quote: Should the marketing authorization holder as a result of the emerging safety issue decide to suspend, withdraw or cancel marketing of their medicinal product, they shall notify the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Obtain MCAZ approval before implementing safety label changes
f.statement: Changes to safety aspects of approved labelling (SmPC or package insert and PIL), and editorial changes, must be submitted to MCAZ for approval before implementation, with a cover letter to the Director-General with justification, tracked and clean versions of the PI/PIL, and proof of approval by a stringent or reference authority if available.

rows.quote: Changes to safety aspects of approved labelling information including Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) or Package insert (PI) and PIL must be submitted to the MCAZ for approval before implementation.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Follow the safety communication principles
f.statement: Safety communications should deliver clear, accurate, consistent messages tailored to the audience at the right time; be part of risk assessment and minimisation; be coordinated with authorities; present risks in the context of benefits with seriousness, frequency, risk factors and reversibility; address uncertainties; use appropriate quantitative measures (absolute risks); be pre-tested where possible; be followed up where relevant; be evaluated for effectiveness; and respect data protection.

rows.quote: Should deliver relevant, clear, accurate and consistent messages and reach the right audiences at the right time for them to take appropriate action.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Obtain MCAZ prior approval for every safety communication
f.statement: All safety communications issued by the MAH shall receive prior approval from the Authority; the application shall include a copy of the proposed communication, the distribution medium and the target audience(s). Communications should be effective and systems should be in place to measure their effectiveness.

rows.quote: All Safety Communication issued by the market authorisation holder shall receive prior approval from the Authority.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Agree DHPC content and communication plan with the Authority
f.statement: Preparation of a DHPC involves cooperation between the MAH and the competent authority, with agreement on the content and the communication plan (recipients, timetable and dissemination channels).

rows.quote: The agreement will cover both the content of the DHPC and the communication plan including the intended recipients, the timetable, and the channels for disseminating the DHPC.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Include the required content in safety communications, objectively presented
f.statement: Safety communications shall not be misleading and shall be objective, and should contain: active substance, brand name and main message at the top; the important emerging information and safety concern; the reason for the communication; recommendations to HCPs and patients; background; any statement of agreement with the Authority; proposed product information changes; references; a reminder to report suspected ADRs to MCAZ; and contact details.

rows.quote: The information in the safety communication shall not be misleading and shall be presented objectively.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Be inspection-ready and support PV inspections
f.statement: MAHs/applicants must always be inspection-ready (inspections may be unannounced); maintain and provide the PSMF on request; ensure sites selected for inspection, including contracted firms, agree to be inspected; provide requested information and documents within the deadline or during the inspection; ensure relevant PV staff are available; and implement timely CAPA plans prioritising critical and major findings.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote: to always be inspection ready as inspections may be unannounced;
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Respond to inspection deficiencies with a corrective action plan within 14 working days
f.statement: Following issue of the inspection report, the manufacturer or MAH is requested to respond to deficiencies and provide an appropriate corrective action plan within 14 working days; follow-up continues until the CAPA plan is completed.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.deadline: Within 14 working days of the inspection report
rows.quote: Following the issue of the inspection report, the manufacturer or MAH is requested to respond to any deficiencies identified and to provide the Authority with an appropriate corrective action plan (CAP) within 14 working days.
